newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's past foes join forces to form new party.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's past foes join forces to form new party.

text.p: After years of fighting on opposite sides of the political divide, two South African politicians pledged on Sunday to create a new political movement.

Roelf Meyer, estranged ally of South Africa's former president F.W. de Klerk, and Bantu Holomisa, a popular politician recently thrown out of President Nelson Mandela's African National Congress, told a press conference they now shared a common goal.

"(We want)...to inform the public that the NCF (National Consultative Forum) and the NMP (New Movement Process) are launching a joint committee to work together so as to realise our objective, that of forming a new political party in South Africa," Holomisa, flanked by Meyer, told reporters.
He said the committee would investigate matters of common interest, including strategy, policy and funding, ahead of the establishment of a new movement later this year.
Meyer said, "We need to consult South Africans on policy and our political platform in order to create a party with an an eye to the future, particularly with the vision to the 1999 elections.
"The chief objective in (our) minds is to structure a new political movement which is non-racial."

Meyer, a co-architect of the country's first post-apartheid constitution, quit parliament last month after his resignation from the National Party on May 17, over its resistance to his suggestions for change.
The National Party created apartheid under Hendrik Verwoerd, but decades later under de Klerk it led South Africa's transition to black rule by unbanning the ANC and releasing Mandela from jail.
Holomisa fell from favour with the ANC last year after making public bribery allegations against a colleague and then refusing to apologise.
Meyer and Holomisa said they would talk to other parties.

"We are free now and we don't belong to any political parties. If they do not want to be involved (in the process) now, then there's a view that after we've formed a party together we will then consider a question of forming alliances," Holomisa said.
